newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Feb 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Feb 25.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page Tuesday:
* U.S. Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott suggested creating a commission to make a specific recommendation for fixing the government's main gauge of inflation, the Consumer Price Index.

* The 69-year-old gunman who killed one and wounded seven at the Empire State Building was a Palestinian father from Gaza who had lost his life savings after moving to New York City on Christmas Eve to invest in a new business.

* More than 180,000 immigrants were allowed to enter the United States last year without undergoing required background checks, prompting the U.S. Justice Department to begin an investigation into those cases.

* Gen. Barry McCaffrey, the White House's anti-drug chief, said senior officials have considered downgrading Mexico's rating as an anti-drug ally following recent disclosures about Mexican officials' ties to drug traffickers.
* President Clinton has called for a bioethics advisory committee to examine the implications of genetic cloning after a British scientist successfully cloned an adult sheep named Dolly.
* Researchers have found that the number of New York residents without health insurance has risen to nearly a quarter of the population, up from 20.9 percent five years ago.
